subject: Discovery recap: embeddings & rerank workload (Summit Retail)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@summitretail.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@summitretail.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, Feb 14, 2027 at 4:05 PM PST
Subject: Discovery recap: embeddings & rerank workload (Summit Retail)

Hi Maya / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned on pain, goals, and next steps. See attached sheet (summit_inference_requirements.xlsx) with what I captured from the call.

Pain points we heard
- Current relevancy is inconsistent for long-tail queries; merchandising team wants better rerank precision for low-signal searches.
- Cost and latency: the current hosted rerank path spikes cost and occasionally misses latency SLOs at peak.
- Operational complexity: they maintain a separate FAISS service and a managed vector DB for different use cases.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Embedding model: 1536-d vectors (legacy open model embeddings).
- Vector DB: Pinecone (single-cloud region today).
- Index scale: ~8-12M vectors (most accesses concentrated on a 2-3M hot subset).
- Upserts: nightly full batch (~200k vectors) + streaming incremental updates (Kafka).
- Rerank flow: candidate retrieval -> embedding similarity -> rerank model rescoring (LM-based reranker).

Success criteria (what success looks like)
- Latency: 95p rerank end-to-end <100ms (target ideally <50ms for single-query user flow).
- Quality: +15% CTR or measurable improvement in conversion for A/B test on search results.
- Cost: <= 40% reduction in per-query infra cost (relative to current hosted rerank spend).

Operational notes / workload patterns
- Peak QPS: 35-45 QPS during promotional windows, baseline ~8-12 QPS.
- Batch vs real-time: bulk nightly indexing plus low-latency incremental writes (~500-1k vectors/hour).
- Tolerance for multi-second cold-query: low - customer needs snappy UI.

Redwood approach (high level)
- Suggest evaluating a hybrid: Dedicated inference pool for rerank model + caching (prefix/KV + candidate caches) for the 2-3M hot subset to hit latency targets.
- Recommend experimenting with lower-dim quantized variants for embeddings where recall loss is acceptable to lower memory/cost.
- Consider local FAISS for very cold batch jobs and Pinecone (or PAAS vector DB) for global vector availability; Redwood can route to the right variant by policy.

Next steps (agreed)
1) I’ll follow up with a capacity sketch and a ballpark cost delta (Marissa / Alex) - aim EOD Tue.
2) Summit to confirm exact index size, embedding dim, and a sample traffic day for QPS distribution (Maya).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra and data-platform folks to look at ingestion and caching strategy (Alex + Dev + Summit eng).

Attachments: summit_inference_requirements.xlsx (full notes + traffic sample template)

Thanks - talk soon.

-
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@summitretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir.k@summitretail.com>

Date: Mon, Feb 15, 2027 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: embeddings & rerank workload (Summit Retail)

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the concise recap - this matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Index size is closer to 12M total vectors; our hot set that drives >95% of traffic is about 2.5M.
- Embedding dim is 1536. We have some legacy experiments with 768-d but those weren’t kept in prod.
- Vector DB: Pinecone (single-region for now) but open to moving cold indexes to a cheaper FAISS cluster if it helps cost.
- Peak QPS: on promo days we’ve seen short spikes to ~45 QPS (sustained minutes), baseline 10 QPS.
- Batch: nightly full-ish refresh (200k-250k) and near-real-time streaming updates from Kafka for inventory changes.

Question: for rerank latency - are you expecting the 95p <100ms target to include candidate retrieval + scoring? Our goal is to keep perceived latency under ~200ms for users; we’d like Redwood to propose both a strict low-latency configuration and a cost-optimized configuration.

We’ll aim to share a sample traffic day and the schema for ingestion by tomorrow. Also looping in Gabe (search lead) on the follow-up tech call.

Thanks,
Maya
Head of Search & Personalization
Summit Retail
maya.patel@summitretail.com | (650) 555-3221

Maya - quick follow-up from Redwood on ops & procurement points so we can scope the next meeting: 

- Compliance & security: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and can provide the attestation and network architecture docs. If you need an on-prem or VPC Private deployment, we can share options and timing.
- Cost/config options (ballpark): Hosted (fastest to start) - good for PoC; Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) - better predictable latency for rerank and lowers per-query cost for high throughput; Private - for strict data controls. I attached a short capacity sketch + ballpark numbers (redwood-capacity-proposal.pdf).
- For discovery: would like a short tech-deep-dive (30-45m) with Gabe + platform infra + your search engs to align on ingestion API, streaming cadence, and candidate cache TTLs.

If that works I’ll propose two time slots for next week.

-
Alex Martinez
